tone_statements.quote: From Laycock's 1971 fieldnotes, Busa shows the following features: no morphological plural marking in nouns, no dual forms in pronouns; subject-marking by prefix in verbs, object marking by suffix; verb morphology, and perhaps pronouns, distinguish a third singular feminine subject; nasal vowels occur, and tone may also be present.

tone.says: The only published prosodic remark on the language: from Laycock's 1971 fieldnotes, Busa has nasal vowels 'and tone may also be present' - tone suspected, not analysed; no inventory, no examples.

This is the manuscript notebook of Laycock's Busa (Odiai) field materials, i.e. the most likely primary source behind Laycock 1975: 883 'nasal vowels occur, and tone may also be present'; whether its transcriptions carry pitch/tone marks is unknown until a PARADISEC account holder opens. The OLAC listing for bhf (Internet Archive copy dated 19 Dec 2024) shows no other deposit, recording or phonology item for the language beyond this notebook, Graham 1981 (a work listed here), Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List, transnewguinea.org and a Rosetta Swadesh list.
